utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff, yesterday afternoon you raised a concern regarding the Prosecutor's way of objecting to questions. I indicated at that time that we would take a look at the transcript and perhaps better understand what your concern was. Would you like to reiterate that concern? We have looked at the transcript and we think that we know what objection led to this position that you are taking, but why do you not tell us again?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I will try to do so, your Honour. What I had in mind when I raised the issue was -- I have now had a chance to read the transcript myself -- page 2967 ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Line 21?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: 24, I would say. Miss Hollis raised the objection saying that it was misleading and that "she was never asked if she recognised Dusko Tadic. She was asked if she recognised anyone in the photographs". If you look to page 2968, the next page, at line 11 Mr. Kay resumes his cross-examination and then he asks, "Were you asked when you were shown the book of photographs, Mrs. Jaskic?" Then the witness answered, line 13, "They asked me if I recognised anybody on that photograph". Yes, on that photograph. That crossed my mind when I raised the issue.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What we looked at was, and it relates to the same question but a different portion of the transcript, on page 2967 the question by Mr. Kay at line 21 is: "Did you not tell an investigator for the Prosecution that you did not recognise Dusko Tadic?" Miss Hollis: "Your Honour, I am going to object to this. This is misleading in that she was never asked if she recognised Dusko Tadic. She was asked if she recognised anyone in the photographs". Mr. Kay: "It might be better if we hear the evidence from the witness rather than what the Prosecution believes to have been said".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: "Excuse me, your Honour, but on direct examination the question was: 'Were you asked if you recognised anyone in the photographs?' and her answer was: 'Yes, I was asked that'. That is in evidence". Mr. Kay: "The Prosecution has asked a leading question and sought a reaction from the witness in relation to that question. The Defence are entitled to find out from this witness what was actually said. It seems here that the procedure that has been followed by the Prosecution has provided them with a non-identification and there has been an attempt to try to put this in a positive way, your Honour, which is a proper basis for the Defence to explore what evidence is sought to be brought before the Court by this witness". So it seems to me that, first, Miss Hollis objected to Mr. Kay's question as misleading. Mr. Kay then responds saying, he does not say that it was not misleading, but he says that the question that was asked of Miss Hollis was leading and that, therefore, the Defence is entitled to ask this question. If you go back to the question that Miss Hollis asked on page 2964, line 20, this is Miss Hollis: "Do you recall a member of this Tribunal showing you a book of photographs on that day asking you to look at those photographs and asking if you recognise anyone?" Answer from the witness: "Yes". Question: "Did you recognise anyone in those photographs?" Answer: "Yes". Question: "Who did you recognise?" Answer: "I recognised Dusko Tadic". So, in fact, it appears that Miss Hollis is correct in that the question was: "Did you recognise anyone in those photographs?" The witness says: "Yes", and then goes on, whereas Mr. Kay characterised the testimony on page 2967, line 21, as: "Did you not tell an investigator for the Prosecution that you did not recognise Tadic?" which led to Miss Hollis's objection. It appears that Mr. Kay's question was a mischaracterisation really of the witness's answer. His response was, "Well, it was a leading question. We are entitled to get into it". What we suggest is that if a question is leading, and the question, "Did you recognise anyone in those photographs?" is not leading although the previous question may have some leading components to it, but if it is leading, the way to deal with it is to object to it then, not to mischaracterise the witness's testimony because that is what was done. Do you understand what I am saying or am I talking too quickly?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I accept what you say, but that is not the point I tried to explain to you yesterday. What I tried to explain to you yesterday was that I felt that it was not appropriate to have the witness listening to the discussion as you have just described on pages 2967 and 2968, because the witness from that discussion perfectly understood what she was expected to say. That was my objection. I rather prefer the witness not to understand what was at issue at that time.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You would agree or would you agree that the question was misleading?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, but that was not the point I wanted to make.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. So do you want the lawyers to approach the Bench?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Or have the witness instructed to take off the earphones.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. I do not have a problem with that. Do you have a problem, Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Or Mr. Niemann, rather -- just with this procedure?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour. There is no difficulty with that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. Then we will do that then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: As I indicated, feel free, Mr. Kay, to object if the question is leading ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: --- rather than approaching it the other way. I will instruct the Prosecutor at this time in your response to objections, even though they may be meritorious, attempt to respond to an objection in way that will not clue the witness. If it appears that the witness is being clued, Mr. Kay or Mr. Wladimiroff, then object. At that time we will have the witness take off the earphones -- I think that is an appropriate way to do it -- and hope that the witness does not understand more English than what we think, but we will do the best that we can under the circumstances. Is that acceptable, Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Of course, your Honour. Your Honour, I would please note for the record that I was not attempting in any way to provide an answer for this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No, that is not -- I do not think that was the judgment of the Chamber. It was an appropriate objection. The question is how should it be handled. I think we have explored it enough. Why do we not just get on and continue with the testimony?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. I guess we would have to note for English speaking witnesses we would have to have a different ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I know that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: --- resolution.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You know I am aware of that. I am just pushing that on to another time. We will come up with another way to handle that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Perhaps those witnesses could put their earphones on! Your Honour, yesterday we put into evidence Prosecution Exhibit 292 which was the photo book that was used with Draguna Jaskic. We have made copies of the book. We have provided th copy and the book to the Defence to inspect the book and a copy, and we have copies for each of the Judges. So at this time I would ask that the Bailiff provide this Exhibit and the copies to the Registry.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, would you continue with the Mrs. Mujic's testimony, please?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. I had completed direct examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. All we need is the witness now. MRS. SUBHA MUJIC, recalled.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mrs. Mujic, you understand that you are still under oath to tell the truth that you took yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kay? Cross-Examined by MR. KAY

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Mujic, before the conflict in Kozarac do you know how long Dusko Tadic had had a cafe in that town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You cannot remember when this job of a cafe owner was taken on by him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I do not know when he started. I was not paying attention to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember when a cafe opened at his house in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever spoken to Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or spent any time in his company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to now talk to you about 14th June 1992 when you were at the house of Draguna Jaskic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember what time it was that soldiers came to the house on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around 3 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in the house at the time those soldiers arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The women and men from the house were all taken outside the house at the same time, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some stage the men were separated from you and put by the sand near the barn, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whilst you were still outside you told us that Dule Tadic beat those men from your house whilst you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That happened in front of you whilst you were standing outside the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember what uniforms the soldiers were wearing outside the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Black uniforms, camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by black uniforms that are camouflage uniforms? Can you describe the colours for us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Like dark blue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the top clothing as well as the bottom trouser clothing being dark blue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of them were wearing this black camouflage uniform that was dark blue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. What do I know? I know there were two inside in the yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those two came outside from the house, did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One came out of the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to the other one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He stood guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereabouts did he stand guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He stood near the men and near the entrance to the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were in the house did he stand guard there as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they went out to the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the soldier said that if you watched that they would shoot you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any soldiers then watching you to stop you looking outside the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you not frightened that any of them might see you looking from the window of the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What are we going to be afraid about? Our lives are not more expensive than from our relatives and our husbands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The men who were dressed in this way, can you remember if they wore anything on their heads, if there was any head gear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of head gear was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. They had something over their faces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would that be masks over their faces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of them wore masks like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were not any of the others wearing anything else to disguise their faces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the man you say was Dule Tadic, was he wearing a mask?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The upper part of the clothing of the men, can you remember whether they wore jackets or shirts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jackets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Like military jackets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those jackets have sleeves that covered their arms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, long sleeves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all the men dressed the same, with the same kind of clothing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The ones that I saw, the only one was the one who beat them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was the one who beat them dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The camouflage uniform, a multi-coloured one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that a different colour from the black camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What colour uniform was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Like green, like not a real green, but olive green.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you saw Dule Tadic beating ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: --- the men from your house ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: --- out outside the house is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the road. When you were inside the house, were they in the same position on the road or had they moved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the road lying down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you were outside the house had they already started to beat them on the road whilst you were outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or did any of the beatings start whilst they were by the sand near the barn?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that your sister said, "Look at Dusko Tadic, he's hitting our family, the husband, the father, the brother, everybody, is killing all the family, the husband, the father, the brother, everybody"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that was not happening outside there on the road, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sure it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But she just uttered those words to you? How did she say them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Dule Tadic is killing all of our family, the relatives and the husbands".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was she crying or screaming, distressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How should she not be excited and how should we not have cried, both of us, when he was killing all of them in the row? Would you not cry or would you keep silent?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what you describe, you see, out there, there were no shots being fired out there on the road. It appears to have been beating, kicking and hitting that was happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the house there was shooting which I did not hear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that did not happen whilst you were watching what was taking place in the road, did it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While we were outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was shooting inside your house whilst one of the soldiers was searching it, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the house of my sister.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: None of the soldiers heard any distress from you and your sister?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not bring attention to yourselves whilst you were looking through the window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How should we? They would kill us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you had taken that risk, you told us, because you did not care and that is why ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that is right, that is certainly right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because what I suggest to you is that in fact you did not see this at all as you have described it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only if you can say that we were not there and that it did not happen and that we did not exist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that you did not see Dule Tadic there in Jaskici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you claim to have known Dule Tadic when in fact you did not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us anything more about Dusko Tadic from what you have told us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said what I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour, no redirect.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to Mrs. Mujic being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mrs. Mujic, you are permanently excused. You are free to leave. Thank you for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. (The witness withdrew).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour the Prosecution would call Mrs. Zemka Sahbaz. Mrs. Zemka Sahbaz, called.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Sahbaz. You may be seated. Examined by Mr. Keegan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please state your full name for the record?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zemka Sahbaz.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Sahbaz, what is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 18th February 1949.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the village of Jaskici, the Local Commune of Kamicani near Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that where you grew up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I grew up in the village of Jaskici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you married?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five, unfortunately, four are alive and, well, I do not know what is happening to that fifth. I still know nothing of his lot and this uncertainty is terrible for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am. Where did you live after you were married, Mrs. Sahbaz?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the village of Babici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to the attack on Kozarac in May 1992 did you go to stay in Jaskici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you leave Babici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to my close relatives, to my next of kin. I had my sisters, mother, brothers there. Where I was married there were more a Serb population and, unfortunately, I saw them surround us with weapons of all calibres. We could see the barrels of tanks which were exposed and pointing towards our village directly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Sahbaz, can I ask you when you answer to please speak a little more slowly so that the interpreters can keep up with you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when the shelling of Kozarac started?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the village of Jaskici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do when that shelling began in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was at a loss where to go, what to do, nor did anybody know where to look for shelter when the shells were hitting from all sides and different calibres of fire could be heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did the residents of the village go when the shelling started?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Wandering left and right. We could not go out anywhere as we were surrounded in the fields, in the woods. You did not know where to go, where to turn, where to look, to look to how to save your head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the attack in the Kozarac area began did refugees come to the village of Jaskici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, quite a number of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to Jaskici where were you originally staying, in which house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With my sisters for a while and when it began to overflow with refugees, then a neighbour not far from there, the third house from my sister, she was alone with her daughter and she came to the house. We were afraid that her house would be set on fire because it was shot and she was alone because they mostly set on fire those houses which were empty. So we moved over to her house and were together with her, so that her building would remain intact because we did not know whether we would be able to go out anywhere from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Sahbaz, you see the chart behind you which is Exhibit 287?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could take the pointer -- leave the headphones on, please -- if you could point first to your sister's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is my sister's house where I was during the first day of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could point to where your sister's house is located on the diagram of the street, identify which house of the red squares?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: I cannot see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please speak into the microphone, we cannot hear her really.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mrs. Sahbaz, if you could move on to the side where your witness chair is so that you are closer to the microphone. If you could again point to where on the street map your sister's house is located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is my sister's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the street map, the red squares?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Iso Nureski, that is the husband.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now which is the second house that you moved to while you stayed in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ahmet Jaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could point to the picture of that house that is on that chart?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the house in which I was at the time when the army arrived there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You can take your seat again. What day did the soldiers come to the village of Jaskici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 14th June. I shall never forget the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember approximately what time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember the hour. I only know it was afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the first thing that you remember happening when the soldiers came to the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember first of all we heard a din and gunfire from afar, bursts, individual from time to time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that shooting get closer to the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the village of Sivci which is the adjacent village to Jaskici, the voices were coming ever closer and when we saw that it was coming near our houses we were looking for shelter in the nearest houses so we were all inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you later go outside of the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I tried to come out and I heard a very powerful burst, fire, and I rushed out as if in ignorance to see what was happening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could have this photograph marked as the next Exhibit, please, which I believe is 293, and then handed to the witness. Mr. Sahbaz, do you recognise that picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the picture is quite clear, except that it was not like that but, fortunately, I have had the chance to see the place and the appearance and there is still the entrance of the house. I can tell you where I was standing at the time, where I went out through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose house is that a picture of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a Ahmet Jaskic's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Sahbaz, if you will, using the pointer again and pointing to the picture on the machine, can you indicate where the entrance to the house was? Point out in the picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One entered from the main road into the yard and from the yard, from the lower side, up the stairs into the hallway. This was the small wall. As you can see here there was a hallway. That is the place where one took off one's shoes and such like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can just point to where the stairs were, please, and leave it there for a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The steps were here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You entered ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In front of the entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: --- into the side of that portion of the picture which is white?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came outside where were you standing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were standing by the end of this wall on the steps themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What could you see when you came outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I first looked towards the end of the barn which you can see here, except that it is now overgrown by these shrubs and trees which were not there, which were not there when I was, that I know. This did not exist at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you looked that way what did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We saw an individual in a uniform leading a man by the scruff of the neck holding him by the hand, with one hand by the neck and in the other hand there was a rifle. Next to him was a yellow boy, he had blond hair, he had his back turned on me. I could not see his face.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The man you described wearing the uniform, what kind of uniform was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Camouflage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see that man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the road behind this barn, at the very corner of the barn, except that he was on the road and there was a fence here separating the road from the yard of Ahmet Jaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You can return to your seat now. The man they had by the scruff of the neck, the man from the village, did you notice anything about him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him bloody. His shirt was bloody and the nose, and that is what I saw as I looked towards him. I really would not like to talk about him because of the safety of his parents and things like that. I know the name of the man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The man with the blond hair whom you also saw, was he one of the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know him at all. All I could see was that he had a stick in his hands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have -- what was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am trying to forget it all. I do not want to remember everything. It is very hard on me. I am a mother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand, but as best you can recall, what do you remember him wearing, what kind of clothing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he had a shirt. He had a kind of a shirt. He did not have camouflage clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the colour of the shirt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am trying to forget very many things. So rather than make a mistake, he was dressed like that. What I looked at most were the uniforms of people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What colour was the camouflage uniform that you saw? The man with the camouflage uniform, what were the colours of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Many coloured, motley.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what was the primary colour in it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dark blue and coffee, light coffee, all colours were rather pale.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to those two soldiers, what else could you see when you were near the stairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In front of Salko's house I saw that women and men were outside. They were standing against the wall of Salko's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice any soldiers over there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you recall that soldier wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A black t-shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am sorry to interrupt, I have just noticed we have lost the transcript on our screens. I do not know if this is a technical problem we should attend to -- sorry, Mr. Keegan about this.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kay. We have stopped at "camouflage".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am in the same position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I did not realise it had stopped. (The court adjourned for a short time). (11.05 a.m.)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan, do you know how much we lost?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. I think after that I simply went on to, "Did you see anything else?" and she started describing what was happening across the street at Salko's house. So I will just pick up from there again.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK, that is what my notes show.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think the colour of the camouflage uniforms, your Honour, is the note that I have which follows thereafter.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think you are right. We do not want to clue, but why do you not get back because I have some colours in my notes too, so pick up at that again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I apologise for the technical problem. I am sure you lawyers and everyone understands that we are making the best effort we can. It was interesting that the courtroom was designed, it is a wonderful courtroom, and then the equipment kind of keeps coming in, more and more equipment, so it is difficult sometimes to reconcile it. Under the floors here we have more wires -- sometimes that is my biggest concern that a wire is going to creep up from under the floor. So I apologise, but it is working, I think, pretty well under the circumstances. Anyway, Mr. Keegan, would you continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mrs. Sahbaz, we did miss a couple of incidents so I am going to go back just a couple of questions. The man with the camouflage uniform, I asked you if you could recall the colours in that multi-coloured uniform.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: OK. Again could you state what colours you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dark green and dark coffee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other man, the blond man, do you remember what he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a shirt and trousers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, do you remember anything about those colours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think, I cannot quite decide whether, what colour. I was just mostly watching the head, the face, the head. I was not that interested in the colour of the -- I was sort of confused. I was scared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you were mostly watching the head and the face of which person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The person who was yellow, the man who was in the shirt, and had a stake, with a stake, that person. But his back was turned to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to those men who you saw on the road, did you see any other people in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In whose yard was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Salko's, Salko Jaskic's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see over in Salko Jaskic's yard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Men and women who were lined up against a wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers over there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw one in black t-shirt who had a gun and was standing between Salko's door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The translation says that the man was "standing between Salko's door". What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was in the yard when I was looking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could, please, take the pointer and using the picture of Salko's house on the big board there show where you saw that soldier standing, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right here, this is ----

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Sahbaz?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- this is the kitchen and this was the door and this is where men and women were standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You need to stand back so everyone else can see where you are pointing, please, and that pointer pulls out further. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between the door of the house and the house of the -- the door of the kitchen, the summer kitchen. Here he was standing. He was turning left and right and he was holding the rifle at the ready when I saw him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very good. For the record, your Honour, that is the picture in the lower left hand corner of that chart as you look at it, and the general area indicated would appear to be what looks to be a white door or a white opening in the centre part of the picture.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mrs. Sahbaz?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: The area on the photo you just pointed to is what we are talking about, Mrs. Sahbaz.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The area that we showed of Salko's house. Certainly between Salko's house and the kitchen, and then there was also a barn and they had a well as well. It is all clear. He was moving left and right, but when I first saw him he was there, then later he moved left and right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You can return to your seat now. You indicated before that when you saw the man in the camouflage uniform he was standing on the road basically equal with the corner of the stable to Ahmet's house which you pointed out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw that man there, did you get a good look at his face?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, completely, he was facing directly towards me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he saw you what did he do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When he saw me, before he saw me, he was looking in front of Salko's house. I do not know what else, but when he saw me he cursed my son and he said, "What are you waiting for? Why are you not coming out, all of you?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then what did he do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "If I find anybody in the house, I will kill you all".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he fire his weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He raised the rifle and he shot towards the house. I do not know if it was up in the air or on the roof, I cannot interpret that, but I heard the noise of the rifle and I was -- I had already turned my back, I walked into the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you walked into the house, did ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Everybody was excited in the house. They saw what was going on. They were looking at me. They were pale faced. They were scared. I said, "We have to come out".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was in that house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were all women and my son who was 19.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did everyone go out of the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We all came out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go tell your son to come out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My son came out too, my daughter told him, "I was too afraid, I did not know where I was". I came out first. I came, I stepped next to the corn barn and I do not know where everybody else. So I was first next to Ahmet's gate and then behind me the rest followed. I was closest to the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could have the Elmo turned on again, please? Mrs. Sahbaz, again looking at the picture of Ahmet's house, can you using the pointer ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: --- on this machine indicate the general area where you were standing when you came out that second time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can. When I came out this door, I came towards here where these poles are. Now the corn barn is not there any more. I stood here next to this pole which has remained here so that the truth can be proven, and the rest were lining up. I do not know whether they were towards the house or where, I do not remember, but I only speak what I remember, from my memory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You can return to your seat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came back out that time, what was happening on the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw men who were there in Salko's yard. They were all on the road already and they were lying down on the ground, across, the one next to another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to the men from Salko's house, were there other men also there from the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were refugees. I was not at that time watching it. I did not know them. The ones that I know are the ones who are from those houses. Everybody was at home in that village, the inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The man with the camouflage uniform, where was he at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was still standing next to the barn but on the road, Ahmet's barn by the road, and he was standing on the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you then see happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw he nodded. He just pointed to the yellow one who had a stake in his hand. He just did not say a word, just pointed with his head, and this blond man took the stake and started beating up on people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: OK. This blond man, which people was he beating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The ones that were lying down in front of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How big was this stick that he had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately, as I saw, I did not measure it but just looking, he, it was going over two men and was reaching the third man, this. As people were lying down he was beating over them, over their backs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How hard was he beating these men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He beat with as much force as he had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the men screaming when they were hit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some that were not being beaten were silent and those who were hit, they were groaning and they would raise their heads a little bit and then their legs a little bit, but their stomachs were on the road where the blow came as if they were arching, and then it would come back to the ground afterwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this time, this beating, did you look at the man in the camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was watching that person the whole time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were you paying attention to the man in the camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never knew that a time would come when I would have an opportunity to say something like this. I did not believe it, that I will live to see that, and I personally watched because of that, so that they would execute the order that he was giving.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The man in the camouflage uniform was giving orders to the others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was observing that the whole time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He turned into Ahmet's yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who turned into Ahmet's yard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The person who was in the uniform, and told us to go into the house, all of us, in front of Ahmet's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you all get into the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As we were coming into the house, we walked one by one. That is how he told us. As we were walking in, as my son was at the doorstep, maybe two more steps to get into the house, he turned around and looked to the road, towards the persons who were already on the road, and he just walked back, just the same person who was in the uniform, "Just come here".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: OK. When your son turned around and looked towards the road what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He called, the person who was standing in the uniform asked my son to come to the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your son then go down to the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My son, because somehow he came out bare foot and he bent down to pick up the Adidas shoes that were there to put them on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While he was putting his shoes on, did he say anything to you about the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were beaten continuously, the person who was there, they kept on beating them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While your son was putting his shoes on, did your son say anything to you about the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not say anything to the soldiers. He just whispered to me in a low voice, "Mama", as if he was less afraid, "Mama, I know one of them". He was very pale. He was very frightened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your son indicate which one of the soldiers he knew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not show it. He just said, "The one in the black t-shirt, that is the one I know".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you anything about this soldier, about how he knew him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "When I went to school he was watching our tickets, he was checking our bus tickets".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your son was telling you that the soldier worked on the bus that he took when he travelled to school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After your son got his shoes on and began to leave the yard, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I followed him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you follow him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went, I almost went to the gate. I do not know what was happening to me. I am not letting go of my child, whatever happens to him will happen to me. My son is then leaving at the gate and I was about three metres away from him. Somebody called out, called him out. There was the hedge, it was trimmed. Then there were canals that were dug out. So the road is much lower than the hedges. Somebody called him and said, "Come on, forward". I did not see the man. I just heard a voice as he says, "Come forward".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your son then head up the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, towards Kozarac, along the road that is the road that leads to Kozarac, Kamicani/Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to you in the yard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The person who looked at me, I was already at the gate, I was close to him, three or four metres, he kicked the fence with his foot, the fence that was separating Ahmet's yard and the road. He kicked the fence and the fence fell into Ahmet's yard and he cursed my mother and he said, "Bula, have you come to recognise somebody?" He raised his rifle. He did not shoot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which man was it that did this, that kicked the gate and pointed the rifle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The one who was in the uniform standing by that same road, by that gate in the camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My daughters ran over and ran into the house and I simply was completely lost. I did not know where to go, where to turn and I would let him shoot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whilst I was at the entrance, I paused by that window, by the window of this entrance. My legs were trembling. I simply could not go on. There I stopped, looked once again. People were, people were lying there on the ground, were still being beaten and I felt sick, and I know nothing else. My daughters took me to the house for a while. I was completely unconscious and I did not know anything, where they went, how they went, what happened in front of Ahmet's house. I do not have any words about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if that would be a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Let us continue for 15 minutes and see if, perhaps, we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Very well, your Honour. Mrs. Sahbaz, do you have any idea how long you were in the house after you went in ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not, I do not remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you later go out of the house again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I heard cries of pain almost in front of the house on the road between Ahmet's and Salko's house, then I came out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came out what could you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw Abaz Jaskic's two daughters, they were tearing their hair off, each one her own hair, and crying. Between them was blood of those individuals who had been beaten there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go down to the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I started on the road towards Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you first got to the road between Ahmet's house and Salko's house, what did you see on the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I started up the road and I came near my sister's house, near Dzemila's house, and there I saw bodies of dead people on the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described that when you first came out of the house you saw blood on the road.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in front of Ahmet's house, between Ahmet's and Salko's house, where they had beaten those people, the blood remained where their heads had been. Their heads were turned towards Salko's yard and house and their legs, their feet, were towards Ahmet's house. That is how they had lain down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any evidence of anything else on the road besides that blood where the men had been laying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember even how I reached my sister. I do not know. We were totally bewildered. We were totally confused. There was nobody to ask. You simply looked how to survive yourself, and we were scared. We did not know who was where because one could hear shots from every side. There was a lot of din.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did part of the road look wet like water had been splashed on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what we heard. I did not see it, but I was told that by the younger generation, and none of the women talked about that, but those who could bear it all, that is, those younger, little girls and little boys, they had taken a pot which was full of water next to the well, the bucket which was next to the well, and they poured it over people so as to help them stand up. But they told me, I did not see it. I only saw that the road was wet, and I saw blood, that is, I saw it was damp and bloody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see that the road was wet and damp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right there between Ahmet's and Salko's house where people had lain on the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you headed up the road in the direction of your sister's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the direction of the road also to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to the two bodies that you saw on the road, did you see any other bodies that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Behind Ilijaz Elkasovic's house there were more bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit 285, please? Mrs. Sahbaz, I would like you to look at this list of names. Please keep it flat on the table while you are doing so. Do you recognise the names on that list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I do. Not all, but I recognise because they were refugees whom I did not know, and on this first page I know all those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you first tell us, please, by the number or letter the man whom you saw come up the road with the bloody face when you came out of your house the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just a moment. No. 7.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which of those names, again by the letter or number, do you remember being in the group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: OK. Next I would like you to indicate by the number or letter the men whom you saw laying on the road who were being beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, No. 1, No. 2 and No. 7. These are the three men I saw being beaten up before my very eyes. Others I did not. I could not, nor did I look.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether or not in addition to those three there were other men laying down on the road being beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I do not remember. I cannot recognise people as they are moving away from that gate and I cannot see them. They are going up the road. There is a hedge and you cannot see farther than that. It is only those three that I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you again indicate on that list by the letter the identities of the bodies which you saw that day in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Letter A, B, C, D, E -- these are dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, can you list by the number the men whom you know were taken from the village of Jaskici that day?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. 13, is that your son?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is why I stopped. I saw his name and my hands started trembling that he is almost the last one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In May of this year were you shown a book of photographs by an investigator from this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the investigator say to you when he showed you that book?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He asked me if I could recognise any one of those pictures he would show me in the album, "Do you know them"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the pictures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of all the pictures I picked out only one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the man that you recognised? Where had you seen him before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had seen him in the yard of the road between Ahmet's and Salko's house. That was the individual who was in the camouflage, in the mottled, in the multi-camouflage uniform. That was a person I could recognise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sign the back of that picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was sure that that could be that person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could have this book marked as the next Exhibit, please? It will be 294 and then shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Sahbaz, can you please look at that book and then tell me if you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognise this book. It was with me and I looked at all those pictures. This is the picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you turn that picture over, please, and tell me whether or not your signature is there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only if I take the picture out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I would offer Exhibit 294.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 294 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I think I may have omitted to offer Exhibit 293 as well, the photograph of Ahmet Jaskic's house. I would offer that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 293 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mrs. Sahbaz, have any of the men who were taken from that village that day been heard from, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One heard about and, lamentably, nothing I could learn directly, to talk directly to that man, one of them survived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you heard from or seen your son since that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never. I have not heard my son, but I heard an individual who had gone with that group that survived, and about my son what I heard several statements that he was alive and he was coming to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But have you ever heard from him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for 20 minutes. (11.45 a.m.) (Adjourned for a short time) (12.05 p.m.)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Counsel realises that we will not be hearing this case tomorrow. We will resume on Tuesday of next week at 10 a.m. after we conclude today's proceeding, of course. Mr. Kay, cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Cross-examined by MR. KAY

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Sahbaz, did you know Dusko Tadic of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The photographs you were asked to look at in May of this year, you wrote on the back of the photograph that you identified the date when you looked at them, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what I have seen, that was 31st May of this year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 31st, yes, but I do not remember the month, whether it was May or another one, but the date, 31st, yes. I omit a lot, I do not remember everything, but I remember the date, 31st, my signature, but I do not remember the month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Had you seen any of these proceedings on television before you looked at that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, absolutely. I do not have the satellite dish. I have no opportunity to watch. I am on the countryside in (redacted) and there are only four Bosnian families and we do not watch. If I can go to any of the (redacted) people, that is impossible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you see any of the news concerning this trial on the television of the country where you are living?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On television we did not, only on radio, sometimes we listen. I do not want to listen. It is difficult for me. I am a mother and I avoid the news. It is affecting, as you say, my nerves. I cannot tolerate that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you do have a television where you live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have television but I do not have satellite, so I cannot watch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the ordinary television, not the satellite stations, the ordinary television that is put out in the country where you live, do you receive that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whilst the news ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember. I rarely watch television. We go on walks. My husband was in three camps. He is excited all the time. He does not want to see or hear anything. There is a fifth year that our son is missing. We are still uncertain. He has not seen his mother for five years. He does not know whether she is alive, and if I should go to watch the news I am not interested in that. I just save my head. I turn away my head so that I do not watch what is going to be the dead bodies and all that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But have you had on the television news about this trial, when it started?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not believe that I would come, that I would be on television to say something, but I am not interested in what other people say, only what I need, what my interests are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anything in newspapers about the case of Mr. Tadic? Have you seen anything in those newspapers in that country where you are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen anything ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not hear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: --- in the newspapers of that country where you live about this case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not read papers. I cannot read papers. I cannot see. I do not have the glasses. I have been crying all the time. When I have to see a picture, I am asking for a pair of glasses and I absolutely do not read papers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any photographs of Mr. Tadic in the newspaper that you have seen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not buy papers and I do not follow papers, absolutely, only pictures, photographs that I get from somebody, from my family. For that I am looking for glasses, nothing else and then I borrow them. I do not own one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. If I can ask you some questions then about that afternoon of 14th June 1992. You told us about the Serb soldier in the camouflage uniform who was leading a man by the scruff of the neck up the road towards your house, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it right that the man who was being held that way was Ismet Jaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Personally, Ismet Jaskic, son of Huso Jaskic, that is my uncle's son, and I watched him bloody, in the hands of a soldier with a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that man have a hat on his head as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first time I saw him he looked as if he was from head to tow in the camouflage uniform, and I believed that he had something on his head, some kind of protection. That is what I reckon was on his head. That is the sense that I had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember him wearing a camouflage hat with a wide brim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It was all one colour, that uniform, multi-coloured, as the uniform. It was just as a shield from the sun. The second time when I came out, I do not remember anything. I was just -- I do not know what was on him. I was just following what he was saying because I was scared. I was very scared. I was in fear all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said that he had a shield from the sun, is it right then that you remember this man wearing a hat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do remember this man wearing a hat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember. I think he had for a while, after that I do not remember anything, but I remember that man personally and his face, and the whole time I was looking not to forget it. I did not want to remember it but I cannot forget him, what fear I went through and what I saw there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we can just consider the hat for the moment, was that a camouflage hat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not observing the head. I could not go around to survey it. You can only look at the person. When you are quiet and when you are in fear, you can just account for the moment you are in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember though that hat having perhaps a wide brim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you have given descriptions of this man, have you in the past referred to him as being the man in the hat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The camouflage uniform you told us about, earlier this morning I understood you to mention that it had the colour blue inside it with coffee and pale colours as well as being dark, a dark blue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Green colour, dark green and coffee, which I imagine and what I saw, and you can say whatever you like, that is your opinion is that, and my mind is this, as I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was just wondering because I was using your words from earlier this morning that you said it was dark blue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dark green.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that just a mistake this morning if you said that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not for me. Not my opinion -- not a mistake, in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you say this man and you looked into his face, can you remember if he had a beard or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember a beard, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other man you have described, the blond man, he was the man with the long stick, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had -- it was not a stick, it was a stake, what you pull out of the fence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember the colour of the clothes that he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am trying to forget everything else. I remember the head and hair. He was turned -- his head -- back was turned to me. This is what I remember. He was not turning his face to me. As long as I watched, he was turned to the back. He was facing Salko's house and the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I am sorry. Pardon the interruption, your Honour, it is a redaction matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: The time code is 12.11.42 which, I believe, was page 57, line 6 perhaps. Then I believe right after that there was a second, within a sentence or two. The second one is 12.11.52, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to those redactions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: They will be granted. Mr. Tadic -- I mean, Mr. Kay for Mr. Tadic. You do not have a beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember any other caps or berets that were being worn by the soldiers that were there in Jaskici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From that day my child is in my thoughts, and that case that I experienced, that is what I think about, and the persons who behaved in what way, I was not observing a lot, just the person most, the most who was in the uniform, and the others I was not that interested in because everybody was looking at him for orders to see what to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the man with the hat with the wide brim was giving the orders to the others, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no white shield. I did not see any white shield.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Hopefully, I did not say that but ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It is a problem with the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I will ask that question again. That is right, you are saying that the man with the hat with the wide brim was the man who was giving the orders to the others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whether there was a brim or not, I do not know, but he was giving orders. It was a shield like for the sun. It was, you know, this is what I saw. But briefly after that I do not remember anything, whether he had it or not. It is not that he was hiding his eyes, that is all I saw, and then like the uniform, camouflage. Everything was the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the hat was a camouflage hat, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right, like, like the rest of the clothes, except it was not a hat, it was more like a shield.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any of the soldiers with a red French beret?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one, I remember in Salko's yard, but as I watched very little, I saw that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any others with red berets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not. Just one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of the ones in black t-shirts wearing red berets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did not, no, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is all I ask, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan, any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to Mrs. Sahbaz being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mrs. Sahbaz, you are permanently excused. You are free to leave. Thank you for coming. You are free to leave, thank you. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would call Senija Elkasovic to the stand. MRS. SENIJA ELKASOVIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mrs. Elkasovic, would you please take the oath that is being given to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. (The witness was sworn)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. You may be seated Examined by MR. KEEGAN

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Elkasovic, could you please state your full name for the record?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Senija Elkasovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 28th January 1961.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Brdjani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that in the opstina Prijedor in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you grow up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the village of Brdjani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also go to school there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, to Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you married?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were married where did you live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the village of Jaskici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a man named Dusko Tadic from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For approximately how long have you known that man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, about 15 years or so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew him from Kozarac because he was -- he married from the village of Vidovici.
