utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before he was married did you know who he was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before he got married I knew him, I knew his face. I did not really know his full name. But when he married Mrs. Mira, then I came to know who he was and what he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to his getting married, when you came to know who he was, what did you mean when you said you knew him by his face?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, you know, from Kozarac by sight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know his wife, Mira?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know her?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because we lived close to each other and we almost grew up together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Vidovici a part of Brdjani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you live close to Mira when you were children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were -- we lived near each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you find out Dusko Tadic's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I learned that, well, when he and Mira got married.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever personally meet Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, only in passing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you on occasion exchange greetings with he and Mira?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said "Hello", "Good afternoon", "How are you?" in passing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where would you exchange those greetings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, say, depends, in Kozarac if we were to meet there, in Vidovici and like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where Dusko Tadic and his wife, Mira, lived in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. In Kozarac they lived across the pharmacy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what Dusko Tadic did for an occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a karate -- engaged in karate, and he had his coffee bar, coffee bar, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what Mira Tadic did for work in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, she was in the dispensary. She was a nurse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether they had any children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they had two daughters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the war did you ever see Dusko Tadic with a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the war, yes, I used to see him with a beard, without a beard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could I have Exhibit 269 shown to the witness, please? If that could be placed on the Elmo, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is ----

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. With the Elmo switched on, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dusko Tadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the other person in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Emir Karabasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know Emir Karabasic, Mrs. Elkasovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was also in Brdjani and I would walk past his house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall when the war started in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 24th May '92.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when the shelling started?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the shelling started, I was in my field, I was digging there, working with the corn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do when that shelling started?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My husband came and said, "Leave that, get away".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did the people in the village of Jaskici go during the shelling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they all went to look for shelter, home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they go to any particular homes in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it depended how they managed. Some went to Abaz Jaskic. Those who were closer to Sivci, fled to Sivci and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why would they go to Abaz Jaskic's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because it was the most solid house that there was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did the others flee to Sivci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it depended where each one of the people were, I mean, so they were escaping. We were not all in one and the same place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you stay in those places where you escaped to the whole time or did you return to your own homes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That day I spent there all the time and then we went to Sivci and then again came back home. So that we went to Sivci and to Abaz's house and back to our homes until the shelling stopped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to Sivci where would you stay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to, what's his name, to Sadik Sivac's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you go to that particular house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was also a solid house, a big house. There were many of us there and that is why we went there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Over the next few days while the attack in Kozarac was ongoing, did refugees come to your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, they came to -- the refugees to me, my parents, mother, brother, sister-in-law from Brdjani came to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the other houses in the villages, did refugees also coming to those houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in all the houses, whoever had somebody, refugees came to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did those refugees come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, let us see, there were refugees from Brdjani, from Kamicani, from Jakupovici, from Kozarusa, Besici, from all over the place. Whoever had kin there, they came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the ethnic group of those refugees who came to your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That of the other families that lived in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Our village?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In our village they were Muslims. There was only one household, a Ukrainian one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which house was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was Jozo Orlovski's household.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the day that the soldiers came to Jaskici, how many of the families who lived in Jaskici left the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From four houses when the cleansing passed, in five houses there were still people in them. Huso Jaskic's family left all. He stayed alone in the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any checkpoints in the village or near the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of the men of the village patrolling the village with weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean our men?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What day did the soldiers come to the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 14th June '92.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately, what time did they come?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometime between 2.00 and 3.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the first thing that you remember happening when the soldiers came to the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first thing I remember was a shot fired behind my house. It was very close. My husband came out to look from the bedroom, and when he looked he saw the army coming to the house and he said, "Here they come". Then all of us who were there, we stood up, we jumped up. My child was asleep at the time, so I went to him. I took the child, and we started for the hallway to come out at that moment, but before that we heard them shouting, "Is there anyone at home?" and we shouted "Yes". We shouted back, "Yes", and we started for the hallway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Elkasovic, when your husband looked out of the window after hearing the shot, where would he have been looking towards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the direction behind my house, towards the field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: OK. Was there a village on the other side of that field?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a forest behind the field and then the village of Sivci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could, please, using that pointer which is next to you on the table, point on the chart there which house is your house, that is Exhibit 287?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the chart] My house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Elkasovic, if you could step back away from the diagram, please, so people can see where you are pointing and if you could also point now ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: --- on the street map the red squares which house is yours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the chart]. This.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just for the record, on those pictures that you see in that diagram which is the house of Jozo Orlovski?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You can return to your seat. Do you know what the nationality of Jozo Orlovski was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jovo Orlovski, who is that Jovo?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Jozo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jozo, well, from what I know, he is Ukrainian, but I do not know much about these things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you started down the hall after someone yelled whether there was anyone in the house. What happened next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, when we started, I saw two barrels from my entrance, from my front door, and then, of course, all of us, women and children and men, and then a soldier, "Women and children back, men forward".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you saw two barrels from your entrance, what kind of barrels?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, they were rifles but I know nothing about rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those rifles were pointing into your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Into my hallway through the one that we were trying to come out of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the soldier then yelled, "Women and children back, men forward", what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Men stepped out. We returned into the hallway and a soldier followed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could have this photograph marked as the next exhibit, 295, and then handed to the witness? Mrs. Elkasovic, do you recognise that picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognise it. It is my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May that be placed on the Elmo, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Elkasovic, could you first indicate, please, where the entrance to your house was, the front door as you referred to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here, where these people are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As the men from your house went out, you say a soldier came in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which men left your house that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My husband, Ilijaz Elkasovic, my brother, Senad Majdanac, my brother-in-law, Fehim Turkanovic, left the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the soldier came in, what did he tell the women and children to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He shouted and said, "Quicker, you must all go down to the floor and that is where you will stay", women entered -- as they arrived one by one, so we entered. I entered my kitchen and I went to the window. As I was coming towards the window, I looked through it. I wanted to know where individuals from my house were going. As I was looking to where they were going, I saw Dusko Tadic standing in my yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Elkasovic, if you could, please, on the picture indicate which window it was that you were looking out of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph] Out of this window.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, your Honour, that would be the window on the right as we look at the photograph. Thank you. As you entered that room and were looking out of the window, what were you being told to do by the soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said that I had to lie down too. I was carrying the child in my arms, so I laid the child beside me and went down too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you looked out that window did you get a clear view of Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, very clear and very near.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you indicate on the picture approximately where he was standing when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So the entrance into my house was here and men were coming here towards the middle, and there was, somewhere here was the exit to the road, and Dusko Tadic was more or less standing like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, approximately in the centre of the grassy area of that picture as we look at it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the men who came out of your house pass in front of Tadic, that is, between Dusko Tadic and the window that you were looking out of or on the other side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They passed in front of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they passed between Dusko Tadic and the window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in the house and they were outside. They walked past by him in front of him. They passed in front of this window. They went by this window like this, say from here to here. That is how they went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when the men walked by, did they block your view of Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw in person, he was turned towards the window as he was meeting them.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan, would you ask the witness to point again the way that the soldiers came? I glanced away and did not notice it. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: OK. Mrs. Elkasovic, could you please indicate again how the men came out of your house and exited your yard, left your yard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were coming from here where the entrance was and there was a path here to come out. That is my exit to the road. From here they went in this direction and Mr. Tadic was here. So that from through this window here, I saw with my own eyes the person whom I recognised, and a soldier who was following them had his back to me so I could not recognise him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The soldier who was escorting the men from your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was following the three of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the men were leaving your house what was Dusko Tadic doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, then I had to lie down and I do not know what happened next. I mean, the only look I got was when I looked through the window. That was the only glance I had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the time I am referring to. When you saw him what was Dusko Tadic doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall how he was dressed when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a many coloured suit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by a "many coloured suit"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, you know, their mottled clothes, camouflage, those of many colours, military.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it a uniform or civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Uniform, military, army uniform of their -- that uniform. I mean, they all had clothes like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What colours? You indicated that it was multi-coloured camouflage, what were the colours in that uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, listen, what were those colours? Those colours were, you know, something between coffee and coffee with milk. I mean, how shall I explain it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall any other colours other than this coffee colour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, you know, some were lighter, some paler. There were those many colours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you laid down, what was the next thing that you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I laid down on the floor the soldier that entered the house with us walked around over us, looking for money, for jewellery, opened our wardrobes, emptied drawers. So he walked around the house, yelling, shouting. Then I heard from the road a lot of noise, screaming and such like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the soldier who was in your house say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He insulted us. He said that this was not our place, that we were not going to be there, that we were to be off to Turkey, cursing our mothers, abusing us in all sorts of ways.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything about looking at him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he said, "Who looks at me will have her throat cut".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything about what he would do if he found anyone else in the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he went around, searched. He went out in the hallway, around the rooms, "Is there anybody hiding? If I find anyone, I will cut his throat, I will kill him".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get an opportunity to see what that man was wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had, he also had that multi-coloured clothes and the military boots, and a big knife suspended on his belt and he had a sort of a red cap on his head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall what colours were in the multi-coloured clothes that he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am telling -- to tell you that I really don’t remember his colours, you know, I did not have much time to pay any attention. I know it was also various colours. It was also somewhere between coffee and coffee with milk.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan, we will stand in recess until 2.30. (1.00 p.m.) (Luncheon Adjournment) (2.30 p.m.) PRIVATE

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan, would you continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mrs. Elkasovic, when we broke for the lunch recess we were talking about the colour of the camouflage uniform which you saw Mr. Tadic wearing. Could I have Exhibit 139 shown to the witness and have that photograph brought up on the monitor, please? I appreciate that it is a little bit difficult to see on the monitor. I will have the photograph delivered to the Bench once the witness has dealt with it, your Honour. Mrs. Elkasovic, is the camouflage uniform which you saw Mr. Tadic wearing of the same type of colour you see in the one in that picture, Exhibit 139?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What colour was the camouflage uniform that Mr. Tadic was wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Green-ish colour and white coffee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could I have that photograph delivered to the Bench, please? Mrs. Elkasovic, when you and the other women in your house were lying down on the floor, did you hear anything happening outside the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What could you hear, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard some noise, voices, shouts, and I heard where some soldier yelled, "Don't lift your head", and at that point the shots started. However, my mother got up to sit down and said, "They are killing them", and then the soldier that was in my house came and ran over to her and pointed, turned a rifle around and said, "Lie down where you are or else I will kill you, I will cut your throats". Naturally, she had to go where she was originally, and so on.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Can you hear the witness? Perhaps the witness should speak up just a little bit and Mr. Bos maybe .....

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mrs. Elkasovic, did you know when the soldier left your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I assumed that he left when I heard that you could not hear the steps around the house any more. Then I imagined that he may have left. Then I crawled to the door, and I looked out around the hallway and looked into the room and saw that he was not there. Then I went back and I rose up to the window and looked towards the road, what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What could you see when you looked outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw that the military and the people who lived there, that they are moving away from my house. They were going away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which direction were the men moving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They went down the road. I saw them by the house of Zijad Elkasovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what direction were they moving past Zijad Elkasovic ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could, with that pointer indicate on the map of the street in which direction is Kozarac from the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We cannot see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If you could just step a little bit from the diagram when you do that so that the people on the other side of the room can see? For the record, your Honour, I would indicate the witness has indicated as you look at the chart upward in the direction towards the word "Jaskici" from the house marked Zijad Elkasovic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you. You can return to your seat. Did you recognise any of the men from the village who were in that group which was leading?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I recognised two young men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How could you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By their shirts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go outside right away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that moment I sat down where I was. I do not know how much time passed when I got up and went to the yard. When I came to the staircase, I looked towards the field behind the house. I saw two men lying down in my vegetable garden. I did not understand that the people were dead. I just went into the yard. When I came to the yard, I first looked down the road. Then I looked in the direction in which the people left. When I looked in that direction where people left, I could not see anybody. There was nobody there. Then I went alongside the hedge towards the house of Zijad Elkasovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see when you got up towards the house of Zijad Elkasovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First, I saw one dead body. I moved a bit farther. I saw a second one, and then I just collapsed there and I stayed there. How long I was there, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise those bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they men from the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were the men from our village, not all from the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see how those men had been killed? Could you tell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From bullets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see where they had been shot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first body that I saw, he was killed from the back. The other body that I saw, he was killed through the forehead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first man, when you say he was killed from the back, do you mean he was shot in the back of the head?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you collapsed in the road. What is the next thing that you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember that somebody was calling me out, "What are you doing there? Get up, move away from there". I could not get up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was it that was calling you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My father-in-law, Zijad Elkasovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After your father-in-law came to you, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He helped me get up. I went back into the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not go to check on those men that you saw in the garden behind your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that moment, no, but the family of the killed ones arrived and started to search, to look what happened to the men, and when they started, then I went along too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to where those bodies were in your garden?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise those men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell how they had been killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were both killed in their head in the back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the soldiers left that day, were any men left in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three old men remained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall who those men were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was my father-in-law, Zijad Elkasovic. It was Huse Jaskic and .....

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, I did not get the second, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Who was the second name? The translator did not get that name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Munib Jusovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I have Exhibit 285 shown to the witness, please? Mrs. Elkasovic, if you could keep that list of names flat on the desk while you are looking at it, please? Do you recognise the names on that list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you first tell us by either the letter or number which men you saw in the village that day who were killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could indicate by the letter or number which is next to their name, which ones?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Letter A killed, letter B killed, letter C killed, letter D killed, letter E killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of those men, which are the ones that you first saw on the road by your father-in-law's house, Zijad Elkasovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Letter A was the first person I saw, letter B the second who were near Zijad's house, between mine and Zijad Elkasovic's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other men who were taken from the village that day, can you indicate by the number next to the name which of those men you know were taken from the village that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A person No. 1, person No. 2, person No. 3, person No. 4, person No. 5, person No. 6, person No. 7, person No. 8, person No. 9, person No. 10, person No. 11, person No. 12, person No. 13, person No. 14 taken away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. 4 is your husband?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. 9, is that your brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. 14, is that your brother-in-law, your sister's husband?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to the bodies of the men who were killed in the village that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, people, the first person, letter A, was first hidden next to the forest from his mother, and B was also moved to the forest, C also, D and E were moved to the forest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Who took those men to the forest, the bodies to the forest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zijad Elkasovic and Huse Jaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did they take them to the forest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they moved them because of the parents, so that they would not look at that, mostly because of the mothers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did they not bury the bodies right away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did not bury them because we could not, we did not dare.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not dare because of the military. The military was coming after the cleansing every day, 10 times a day, almost every hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were the men finally buried, how many days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have to get permission to bury those men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We had to go to Trnopolje, to the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you not go to Kozarac or to Prijedor, to the municipal authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We never saw Kozarac or Prijedor. It was not possible to go there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you speak to at the camp in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I asked regular soldiers who were guarding the camp who we could ask, who we can talk to, to bury the dead bodies. They said, "Go to Kuruzovic".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was Kuruzovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was some chief among them. I did not know of him until then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he give you permission to bury the bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing in writing. He said, "You can freely bury, nobody is going to do anything".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened, in fact, when the bodies were taken to be buried?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we took a cart, we put the dead bodies on it, and we took it to the entrance of Sivci and there was another group of the military there. They asked, "What are you carrying there?" and they were the dead bodies, "We have to bury them", "Uncover so we can see". Then we uncovered. When they saw it, they insulted them. "Why are you digging this? We killed those. They are stink". Then one came over, took a pistol and then put it at Huse Jaskic's temple and the other one shot Zijad Elkasovic between the legs and then they let them go. So they came to mestef in the village of Sivci. Then they dug a common grave, so to speak, and buried them altogether.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Huse Jaskic and Zijad Elkasovic tell the soldiers that they had gotten permission from Mr. Kuruzovic to bury the bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They said that they were told that they could bury them, but they had no paper, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After they told that to the soldiers, did the soldiers let them through to bury the bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, after that abuse they let them go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that after 14th June soldiers continued to come to the village. What did they want?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, after that. They were looking for cars, tractors, fuel, livestock, brandy, whatever they could think of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did they come?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they were coming every day, as long as I was in the house there, at least 10 people, different people, came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did these people say to you when they came to your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They said what they needed, that they had to take, that they will take, that we were not to watch, we were not to follow them around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they ever tell you where they were from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they was looking for a car or a tractor or whatever thing, "Give it to us. You are leaving here. We will keep it for you until you come back. Don't be afraid. I am from Kozarusa". The other one comes and the same story is told, what he wants, asks for a tractor or whatever, "I am from Radivojci and also to keep it for us until we come back". The third one says, "I will keep it for you until you come back. I am from Babici", and that is how it went -- at least they told us that they were from those places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After 14th June, after the soldiers left, how many families in the village remained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After 14th, when men were taken away, that is the day, the 14th, four households left immediately. So that about, we -- about five households of us remained and Huse Jaskic was alone in his house. All his family had left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before 14th June, before the soldiers came on that day, had any of the families left the village or had they all stayed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, nobody left before the 14th, nobody left anything. Until the 14th we were all at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long after 14th June did you stay in Jaskici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the 14th, I stayed for a month, two or three at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The translation says: "After the 14th, I stayed for a month, two or three at home". Can you please explain again how long after 14th you stayed in the village of Jaskici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the 14th, I stayed a month and two or three days longer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you leave the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I was expelled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you expelled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the police say or do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "You are to be out within five minutes and off you go".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they tell you where you were going?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They told us we were to go in the direction of Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did they take you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Trnopolje camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay at the camp in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Four days I was there. On the fifth I left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you leave the camp on the fifth day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they organised buses which took us to Stari Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what that bus ride was like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We were packed into these buses like cattle, as people say. I had to stand all the time and hold my child in my arms. We drove to Kozarac along the main road Prijedor/Banja Luka. There we were stopped by the army. They came on to the bus to inspect. There were about three or four old men with us, with women and children. The soldier entered and when he inspected us all, he cursed Kuruzovic's mother, saying, "Why is he letting those through? We kill individuals like this" and he lets them through. Then we continued our ride towards Banja Luka. Then somewhere around Banja Luka we were given a small bag, a pouch, in which we had to collect money and jewellery. So this pouch went from one hand to another, and whoever had anything on him had to put in that pouch. It, therefore, travelled, the pouch travelled up the bus and down and then the man said, "No, this is not enough" and sent it on its way again. So that if anyone tried to keep something with him, he also had to turn the rest over, so that the pouch went up and down and it reached him and they took it. Then the drive continued.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone die during this bus ride who was on the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A man died on us, somewhere near Vlasic. The bus stopped. The old man was taken out and he remained there on the edge of the forest by the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did this bus ride stop? Where were you told to get off the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They told us, "Some garbage", they said, called, and we were told to get off. That is where we got off and they told us, "Down there are your folk, Alija Tudjman, are awaiting you". So we continued on foot and there was fire. So we reached a big barricade, a big block.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Elkasovic ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And we ----

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: --- I am sorry, could you repeat the phrase, the name of the place where you got off in Bosnian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Garbage yard, dump site, something like that, they said, "smetliste".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You were saying something about a big barricade after you had been forced to walk. What was this barricade made out of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you not go around this barricade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was told that it was mined all around, that I had to go across that barricade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you have to do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, you know, we are in a plight. You know how it is. I took one child. I took him over, returned to fetch my other child. Took my child over that barricade and then went on my way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when you were at that barricade? Did you come across a soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I came across a soldier who said, "Don't be afraid. We are yours".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said, "Don't be in groups. It is better to be -- the groups be as small as can be and that you are spares and that you move as fast as you can because they shell and they kill".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you have to walk for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 40 kilometres -- 40, 50 kilometres. I went on foot. It must have been 10.00 or 11.00. I really did not think about time. We were dumped at that dump site, and around 9 o'clock I reached that school that I was supposed to come to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you left the camp that day, Trnopolje, were you given any water or any provisions on this trip?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those who had water with him, he took it, yes -- I guess they filled something -- those who did not have did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this walk was everyone who was on that bus, the elderly, the women and children, all able to make that walk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, several older people remained on the road and when the night fell the military came with wheelbarrows and took them to something, Fiat, to a small truck or something. They tried to transfer them somehow to Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Elkasovic, you have indicated the picture of your house on the chart up there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, before 14th June 1992 is that the way your house looked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the second storey on that house complete?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The house was complete, everything, the facade all up to the back of the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Elkasovic, have you seen or heard from your husband, your brother or your sister's husband since 14th June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Neither seen nor heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Elkasovic, I would like you to look around the courtroom, please, and tell me if you see the man that you know as Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what he is wearing, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He has a green, a greenish jacket, a multi-coloured tie and a shirt like coffee with milk.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Miss De Bertodano? MISS DE BERTODANO: Yes, your Honour. Cross-Examined by MISS DE BERTODANO

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Elkasovic, I would like to ask you some questions about 14th June 1992. You have told us that on that day some soldiers came to your house between 2 and 3 o'clock, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 14th June between 2 and 3 o'clock soldiers came to our house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first that you saw of them was when you saw the barrels of two rifles at your front door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you heard one of them saying that the women and children should go back and that the men should come out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told us that three men who were in the house with you went out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many women and children remained in the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let us see, there was I with my two children, my sister with one child, my mother with one son who was minor, my sister-in-law, my brother's wife, with her child.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that is some nine people. How old were your two children at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The younger one not yet five, and the elder 10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was the younger child that you had in your arms, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you heard the order to go back, you went into the kitchen escorted by one of the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the soldier following behind you or was he in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, behind me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you the first of that group of nine to go into the kitchen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the last one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you arrived in the kitchen there were some eight people there already?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they doing when you reached the kitchen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some were already lying down, some were about to. It depended. As they entered, so they had to comply with the orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were carrying your five-year old child in your arms. Was that child distressed at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I had roused the child. The child was asleep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You got into the kitchen and looked at the window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Through the window you saw a soldier standing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, through the window I saw who was standing in my yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think, from what you have shown us on the diagram, he was somewhere to the right of you, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as I looked through the window he was in front of the window. I cannot really focus whether left or right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The three men who had left your house were coming out of the door and walking past this soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In front, in front of that man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So further to the right of you than the soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To my eyes, as they were coming out they were more to the left rather than right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. The soldier, you told us today, was standing in the middle of the yard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a pile of sand in your yard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a pile, not a particularly big pile, but there was a pile of sand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was that in the yard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Next to the window, in front of the window, more up there to the left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw this man, you remembered this morning that he was wearing a camouflage uniform which you described this morning as being dark and light coffee colour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I made a slight mistake but it was a greenish and white coffee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is what you remembered this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not now, I always remembered it. Perhaps I said it the other way round.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he wearing anything on his head?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whom do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The soldier that you say was Dusko Tadic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had nothing on his head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw him through the window and then you put your child down on the floor and lay down next to the child, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I saw in the yard those taken away and who was standing there, yes, then I put the child down and I went down on the floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The soldier who was accompanying you came into the kitchen behind you, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I was entering he was following.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was he who told you to get down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was shouting "All down".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some stage after this you heard that things had become quieter and you left the house and you saw the soldiers going away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I felt that this one was not in the house, I first checked and then I returned, looked through the window and I saw them moving away towards Zijad Elkasovic's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long would you estimate that this incident took from the time when the soldiers arrived at your house to the time when you saw them going away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That, I do not know. Those were the most important moments in my life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw the man who you described as Dusko Tadic through the window, was he looking at the men who came out of the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was expecting those men so that he was turned towards the windows and the house, and he was expecting men to come out of the house. MISS DE BERTODANO: I have nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan, redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour Re-Examined by MR. KEEGAN

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Elkasovic, when you saw Dusko Tadic standing out there in your yard, what did you think?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I thought that because I knew that man that he must have known a few people in that village and that what happened would not happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean, "that what happened would not happen"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That there would be no killings, that time waiting already, that I have been waiting for five years and still do not know where they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any recross? MISS DE BERTODANO: Nothing, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to Mrs. Elkasovic being permanently excused? MISS DE BERTODANO: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mrs. Elkasovic, you are permanently excused. You free to leave. Thank you for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at all. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we have a five-minute recess to arrange for our next witness?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess, then we will take our afternoon recess so for 20 minutes, so you may have your coffee, tea, whatever now and then we will come back in 20 minutes. Thank you. (3.25 p.m.) (Adjourned for a short time) (3.45 p.m.)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I call the next witness I would ask that we attend to one matter from the last witness's testimony. In that regard, I would ask that the Court note a correct identification of the accused by the witness Senija Elkasovic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No problem, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Except to the standing objection that you have. Yes, the record will reflect that the witness properly identified the accused.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, one additional thing, it has been brought to my attention, I do not believe that Prosecution Exhibit 295 for identification has been tendered; if not, we would tender that at this time. It was a photograph of the home of Senija Elkasovic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No problem, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 295 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, would you call the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour the next witness is Mr. Vasic Gutic. MR. VASIC GUTIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please take the oath that has been handed to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. (The witness was sworn)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. You may be seated. Examined by MR. TIEGER.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, will you state your name, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Gutic, Vasif.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born 20th June 1965 in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what part of opstina Prijedor did you grow up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I grew up in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you attend school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The primary school I attended in Kozarac, then the middle medical school in Prijedor and then I studied at the medical school at the University of Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you serve in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I served my military duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were your duties in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in the infantry. After the training, I was assigned as a guard on a military object.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your profession immediately before the conflict in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In 1992 I was -- I had passed all my courses in the University in Banja Luka, that is, I was -- I had three exams left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those were interrupted by the outbreak of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were interrupted. The exam was going to be on May 26th 1992, and the fate wanted it that on that day I ended up in a camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you a quick question about the University of Banja Luka where you studied medicine. When you began your study of medicine, did you have professors from a variety of places or who were from a variety of places in former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the University in Banja Luka is one of the newer universities, so that certain chairs were represented by Professors from other universities, especially from Zagreb. We had guest Professors, lecturers, who held courses but also from Tuzla and Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the time your studies were ended or abbreviated in 1992, had that situation changed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the meantime there were changes in the administration of the university so that the guest Professors from Zagreb and Sarajevo were replaced by Professors from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you indicated that you were raised in Kozarac and went to primary school there. Do you know Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I met Dule Tadic as a karate trainer of the school, of the primary school in Kozarac, because I myself wanted to do this sport, but at that time there were no vacancies. I was late in applying. So I was just observing the training of the young karateists, and I was 15 or 16, 15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a teenager, did he represent one of the significant persons in Kozarac for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not then, given that I gave up that sport, so that after that I was not interested in that or in him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you continue to see him periodically in Kozarac over the years that followed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I would see him in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware, for example, when he opened his cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between the time of the elections and the outbreak of the conflict, did you hear that Mr. Tadic did not want Muslims in his cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard when I came back -- when I went to Kozarac, I heard from other people that Dule stated that no Muslim ear would enter his cafe, that Muslims would not be allowed to come in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that cause you to pay more attention to Mr. Tadic on those occasions when you saw him in Kozarac thereafter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that kind of a statement for the Kozarac environment (which was known as a tolerant town) at that time was something, something terrible, that national differences should be made, and that is why this statement surprised me. Then I simply maybe as I was passing by that cafe or in that town, I was paying attention to it, maybe subconsciously to Tadic and to his cafe, because I was really surprised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, were you in his cafe at one point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, in time that statement faded some, and we would -- when we had time or in passing, we would stop by, not often, but myself and my colleagues occasionally would sit down. I myself also sat down outside once or twice. Next to the room inside he had a little bit of a garden so that you could sit. He had a couple of tables and you could sit down there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention to the attack on Kozarac on May 24th 1992. Where were you when the attack began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the moment of the attack I was in the medical centre in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you been working there in connection with your training as a doctor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, given that Kozarac had been given an ultimatum, surrender or shelling, I thought it my moral duty as a student of medicine to potentially help the wounded and the injured in case of the attack, and I went to the medical centre that day to be disposal -- at disposition on that day if, should there be injured or wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the course of the shelling, were you able to determine whether or not the medical centre in Kozarac was being targeted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, after already the first shells were hitting around the medical centre and one of them fell into the yard in front of the medical centre, and a building shook a lot, and we were very afraid. Then the shelling continued of the vicinity. You could hear strong detonations. One of the -- in the meantime, we already received the first patients and we started to work on them. Immediately following that, a shell fell at the very entrance of the yard of the medical centre and it hit a vehicle which was coming bringing in a patient and the driver himself was slightly injured. After that, another shell hit the very corner of the building. The building shook a lot, and most of the glass was shattered. We felt the detonation inside, stopped our work but then continued on, continued to work. We had a lot of work. All this was going on in the first hour practically of the shelling and the attack on Kozarac, even though the medical centre had a flag which had a Red Cross on it, marking it as a medical centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the medical personnel at the centre relocate the medical facility to another part of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we remained that first day still in Kozarac, that whole night, 24th to 25th May, and after that in the morning we moved to Rejkovici in an abandoned motel in order to protect ourselves and our patients from further shelling and to allow people to keep bringing people and not to bring, not to endanger them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the morning of the 26th, did you and any other medical people return to the medical building in Kozarac, to the ambulanta in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the purpose of returning there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That night, 25th or 26th, by radio an officer of the Serb Army, Radmilo Zeljaja, in Kozarac sent an ultimatum through the radio, of course, for all to surrender to the Serb Army. That was in the night, somewhere around 11 o'clock. After that there were consultations between the police, and again the contact was established and it was said that physically it was impossible to inform all the people who have been hiding from all the shelling and Zeljaja said, "All right".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Gutic, let me ask you this question, if I may. Did you return to Kozarac anticipating the surrender on 26th and for the purpose of making medical assistance available to people who might need it in town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we returned back to Kozarac, because we did not have information about what was going on outside, because in Kozarac, and also to enable people, if there were other wounded people, so that we could continue to help them, to continue with our work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you captured or arrested at the medical centre that morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the medical supplies at the ambulanta collected by Serb officials?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they captured us, and then after a period of time they ordered us to gather all the medicine and all equipment and to load it into a military truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to those medical supplies and to those medications?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The officer of the Serb Army who established the radio contact with the medical centre in Prijedor and said, "I am sending you medicine of Muslims from Kozarac for your use".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That day were you taken to Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that day we were then transported farther. First, to the school in Kozarac and then we were taken to Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately, how many other people were collected at Trnopolje camp on the same day you arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say on that day, because after we arrived in Trnopolje we were taken to the medical centre, but the next day when I had an opportunity to walk through the camp, I think there were 4,000 to 5,000 people in the camp itself already that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What age group or groups were these people and what gender?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were of all ages, from small babies, a couple of months old, to elderly people, 70s or 80s. Of course, women, children, men also, all ages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these men, women and children, babies, free to leave the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, nobody could leave the camp, those days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what way or ways were people prevented from leaving the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there Serb forces there, guards or soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The whole camp was guarded by the Serb Army who were placed around and prevented leaving the camp. If somebody would try, they would be returned, turned back or abused.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated earlier that on the first day you were in the medical clinic. Was a makeshift medical clinic established by you and others in the Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the war in that complex, in that school, there already was a medical centre, a medical clinic, where the doctor worked with three assistants and there was a small lab too which was there for offering medical services to the local population there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What medical equipment or medications were available to you and any other medical personnel who were held in Trnopolje camp to treat the prisoner population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we entered into the ambulanta, we saw that it had been broken into and that all the medication was stolen, so we did not find anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated that guards prevented prisoners from leaving the camp. How were the guards at the camp armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The guards were armed with semi-automatic and automatic rifles and the so-called machine guns, M72 type.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point I would like to use the assistance of a video which I believe has previously been admitted into evidence, and ask if the doctor can point to a few locations within the camp facility. So if we could begin showing that video?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you know what Exhibit that is, by any chance? You can locate it and tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I know it is up in the booth now and I would like to identify the number for the Court. Unfortunately, your Honour, I only know the number it is not at the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What is the number?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we stop that, please, for a moment? The Exhibit number I believed it was, I have just been advised, is not correct. We are not sure of the correct number.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: For the video either?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Does the Defence know what video this is that is going to be shown?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: We have seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it might be simpler to mark this as a new Exhibit which will be 296.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Judge Stephen saw a part of it and recognised it and believes it is in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: We have seen it before. It is the one where Mr. Tadic was identified as standing outside on a corner and the logs were not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That was a still. That was a still photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: It looks as if it came from this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Exactly the same spot.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I did not see it on the screen. Let us play it and see what happens and we will handle any objections there are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We take no point.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Thank you. Go ahead. Please play the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (The video was played) Can we stop it here, please? Dr. Gutic, what does this portion of the video depict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here we see the building of the primary school in Trnopolje which during the war was the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were prisoners housed within the primary school building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the prisoners were closed in there. They were sleeping in classrooms, in the hallways, in staircases -- wherever there was room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we continue, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have to notice ----

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sorry, can you stop. Yes, sir, I am sorry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I notice an object which was not there at that time when the camp was there, that small shed. That was built later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: OK. Can we stop here, please? Sir, the building that we have just panned and the left side of which we now see, what was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the building of the store, the food store, in Trnopolje which during the war also served for housing of the prisoners, especially for the women and children who were being prepared for deportation. There was a group of 13 to 15, about 15 children who were brought in at one point to the camp who were captured in a forest near Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we continue, please? Can we stop, please? Just for orientation, in which direction are we now looking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now we are looking in the direction of the railway station in Kozarac -- towards the railway station in Trnopolje from Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at the end of the road we are now looking at is the railway station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is approximately how far away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 400 to 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we continue, please? Can you cut the sound on the video, please? Sir, what does this portion of the video depict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the north side of the school in Trnopolje, of the building which was the camp, with a northern entrance in the middle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we may continue? Can we stop here, please? You mentioned that there were guards preventing the prisoners from leaving the camp. Were any of the guard posts located in the area we are looking at now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, behind this small building, house, that we see in the background, to the north of it there was a military point with a Serb military who protected the exit from the camp from that northern side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we continue? If we can stop for a moment? It looks like we just skipped to another part. Go forward just a bit. Stop here. Again, sir, just for orientation, we are now looking in what direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now we are looking in the direction of Kozarac. The road is leading to Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By this house there, the second house up there, across the street there was another point which controlled the entrance to the camp from the northern side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we may continue, please? If we could stop for a moment? What part of the camp does this depict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the south side of the camp, towards the railway station, at a level of the former warehouses of building materials.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The object which rises in the upper right portion of the screen is what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
